evidence: Cic. Lael. 101: ad calcem pervenīre (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: the goal of a race-course, “anciently marked with lime or chalk; opp. carcerēs, the starting-point”. It is feminine, like calx, lime.
Chalk, “for marking the goal in a race-course” (Lewis & Short).

sources: Lewis & Short: calx · Lewis & Short: creta
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): pp. 47, 51.
